previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a male with a history of dilated cardiomyopathy, type 2 diabetes, chronic kidney disease, and heart failure, was admitted for chest pain and shortness of breath. He was found to have elevated cardiac enzymes and BNP, indicating a non-ST elevation myocardial infarction and acute on chronic heart failure. A cardiac catheterization revealed a total occlusion of the left circumflex artery, which was successfully treated with a drug-eluting stent. During admission, he experienced transient acute kidney injury likely due to contrast and heart failure, hyponatremia, and episodes of non-sustained ventricular tachycardia managed by his ICD and medication adjustment. He was stabilized on optimized medical therapy including dual antiplatelet therapy, high-dose statin, beta-blocker, ACE inhibitor, diuretics, and digoxin. His symptoms improved, renal function normalized, and he was discharged home with instructions on medication adherence, daily weight monitoring, low-salt diet, and follow-up care.

Brief Hospital Course:
PRIMARY REASON FOR ADMISSION:
___ with history of CAD, dilated cardiomyopathy (EF 20%) s/p  
ICD, tachy-brady, HTN, HLD, DM, who presents with brief episode 
of chest pain ten days after DES to LCX and non adherence with 
clopidogrel.  He was given prescriptions for all of his 
medications prior to discharge and his clopidogrel (and 
metoprolol) were hand-delivered from ___ Care Plus.

ACTIVE ISSUES:
# Chest pain in setting of not having clopidogrel s/p recent 
DES: On recent cardiac cath (___) he had 100% occlusion of the  
LCx osteal lesion. Right dominant 2VD s/p DES to LCx, no 
intervention to 60% distal RCA lesion. He had not been able to 
fill his clopidogrel and re-presented after reporting a brief 
episode of chest pain - however, troponins were lower than 
previous and were downtrending. He was initially started on 
heparin gtt which was stopped after he refused PTT checks and 
after discussion with attending given low concern for ACS. He 
had no further episodes of chest pain.  He was continued on 
metoprolol, asa, plavix and atorvastatin. After multiple 
conversations with his pharmacy, it was determined a hold was 
put on his account (unclear why) and this is why his clopidogrel 
could not be dispensed. Prior to his leaving the hospital 
grounds, the clopidogrel was hand-delivered after being filled. 
He and his family were counseled repeatedly about how crucial 
this medication was. He would greatly benefit from support with 
medication compliance in the future.

# Chronic systolic CHF: Ischemic CM. LVEF 20%. with 
biventricular hypokinesis with LV inferior and inferlateral 
akinesis and severe  hypokinesis of the other segments.  On 
recent admission, was diuresed with IV furosemide and discharged 
on torsemide 40mg daily but reported only taking torsemide 20 
mg. He was also previously started on digoxin. His discharge 
weight was documented at 139.2, and his current admission weight 
was only  137.2. Given lower admit weight, unchanged CXR, and 
minimal pedal edema on exam, he was not aggressively diuresed 
with IV lasix and instead restarted on torsemide 40mg daily.

# CKD (baseline Cr 1.3-1.6):Creatinine at baseline. 
  
# Hx Atrial Tachycardia: On previous admission, was noted to be 
in atrial tachycardia with HR in ___. He was started 
digoxin and continued on metoprolol which were continued during 
admission. He remained in sinus rhythm with PACs.

# IDDM: last Hba1c ___ 8.6. Continued home glargine 40units 
daily with HISS. 

# HTN: Normotensive. Continued home losartan and spironolactone. 
 

# HLD: He was not on a statin, likely because he was switched 
from pravastatin to atorvastatin on recent admission and the 
prescription had not been filled. He was restarted on atorva 
80mg and given a new prescription for this statin.

# GERD: Stable. Continued home ranitidine.  

TRANSITIONAL ISSUES:  
-The patient would GREATLY benefit from support in taking his 
medications appropriately as he was without critical medications 
after this last admission. This was emphasized to his sisters 
who will be helping him. He was given new prescriptions for all 
of his medications with the clopidogrel (and metoprolol) 
hand-delivered to ensure he would have the pills available. He 
should have continued med reconciliation with his outpatient 
providers.
